blocking.section: Control plane upgrades (paragraph after the skew table); Binary upgrades > Kubernetes Drain and restart; Verification runbook (During any upgrade row)
blocking.issue: This is what remains of L4X-3. Node upgrades are now paced by a MUST. Ruralz Control replica replacements are covered only by a SHOULD, and the runbook applies a 10% count gate to every upgrade, including procedures the document itself says exceed it. Each replica replacement sends Reconnect (drain), so about a third of the Nodes redial with streams at age 0 and drop out of clusterNodeCount for 10 minutes plus the ramp (target). Step 2 waits only for /readyz, Raft catch-up and a recovered ruralz_control_connected_nodes. Connected count recovers within seconds, but qualification takes 10 minutes. A three-replica upgrade finished inside 10 minutes therefore unqualifies about 1/3, then about 2/3, then nearly all Nodes (hypothesis). This is the near-zero-count failure that Scalability says 'must not' happen: derived ceilings go to the full limit, hot-key GCRA calls grow as 2 x requests x N_serving / N_published, shard breakers open, and co-tenant keys fall back to failureMode. For a derived-ceiling Cluster that ignores the SHOULD, nothing prevents it. The runbook row also cannot pass on documented paths. A Ruralz Control replacement drops the count by about 33%. The declared-ceiling Kubernetes example (10 steps in 7.5 min) restarts every Node's stream within one 10-minute qualification window, so the published count falls toward zero, and with it Scalability's first-seen GCRA budget, min(B x N_serving / N_published, 500 x N_serving) per Cell (target).
blocking.evidence: Control plane upgrades: "Until OQ-scalability-and-distributed-state-14 closes, each replacement unqualifies its Nodes, so derived-ceiling Clusters SHOULD declare per-Node ceilings first." Step 2: "await `/readyz` on 9902, Raft catch-up and a recovered `ruralz_control_connected_nodes`". Kubernetes: "Example      N = 1,000, minReplicas 300, three zones: M = 100, 10 steps, 7.5 min   (hypothesis)"; Node count: "declared ceilings ([T4](...)) need no pacing". Runbook: "| During any upgrade | `ruralz_control_cluster_nodes`; `ruralz_node_degraded_info{reason=\"state_store_breaker_open\"}` | Drops at most 10% (target); no breaker opens |". Scalability: "A Ruralz Control restart, failover or lost replica must not collapse the count ... a near-zero count sends derived ceilings to the full limit, multiplying hot-key GCRA calls".
blocking.fix: In Control plane upgrades step 2, change the SHOULD to a MUST: until OQ-scalability-and-distributed-state-14 (a) closes, a Cluster using derived ceilings MUST declare per-Node ceilings before a Ruralz Control upgrade. If it does not, the operator MUST wait between replica replacements until `ruralz_control_cluster_nodes` has returned to its pre-step value, about 10 minutes plus the ramp (hypothesis), and accept a drop of about 1 / replicas per step (hypothesis). Scope the runbook row so it is consistent: 'Derived-ceiling Clusters: drops at most 10% (target); declared-ceiling Clusters: count not gated, and first-seen GCRA calls stay within Scalability's per-Cell budget (target)'. Under the Kubernetes example, add that 7.5 min applies only to declared ceilings, and that derived-ceiling Clusters take about 100 minutes (hypothesis) at the pacing above.

blocking.section: Binary upgrades > In-place handover (step 5 Steer; Figure 1); Guarantees (ZG-3); Verification runbook (V-3)
blocking.issue: The revised steering step still resets in-flight TCP handshakes, so ZG-3 and the new V-3 criterion 'zero refused or reset connections' cannot hold at load. CBPF selection applies only to new SYNs. A connection whose SYN reached the old listener before the program swap stays as a request socket bound to that listener until the client's final ACK arrives, about one RTT later. Step 5 has the holder swap the program, accept its queue and close its listeners at once. Handshakes still in the SYN queue at close are dropped: the final ACK finds no request socket and gets a RST, unless `net.ipv4.tcp_migrate_req` is enabled. The kernel added that sysctl to migrate exactly these request sockets as well as accept-queue children. Draining the accept queue, which the document relies on, does not cover them. At half saturation with tens of thousands of new connections per second and a 50 ms RTT, each handover resets on the order of a thousand handshakes (hypothesis). Over V-3's 1,000 handovers, or a fleet upgrade, that is the same queued-connection loss that the document cites HAProxy's 155 per million to avoid.
blocking.evidence: Step 5: "**Steer.** Once accepted, the new process listens; the holder swaps each program to select it through `golang.org/x/sys/unix` (`net.ipv4.tcp_migrate_req` is the alternative), accepts its queue and closes its listeners". Figure 1: "Old->>K: swap each CBPF program to select the new sockets, 9901 included" then "Old->>Old: accept the queued connections, close listeners, QUIC flows lost". ZG-3: "An in-place handover refuses no new TCP connection, queues none on a process that may exit". V-3 pass: "Zero refused or reset connections and failed requests".
blocking.fix: After the swap, have the old process keep accepting for a settle interval before closing its TCP listeners, so that handshakes already in its SYN queue complete and are accepted. Use 1 s (target), longer than the p99 client RTT (hypothesis). Also state that where the kernel provides `net.ipv4.tcp_migrate_req`, handover hosts SHOULD set it to 1, which migrates the remaining request sockets (the pack already names it as the alternative). Update Figure 1 by inserting 'keep accepting for the settle interval' between the swap and 'close listeners', add the settle interval to the handover Drain offset (deadline 20 s after steering plus the settle interval, target), and name the residual. With the sysctl off, only handshakes whose SYN-ACK was lost and retransmitted after the settle interval can be reset. Either scope ZG-3 to that residual or make the sysctl a MUST.

non_blocking.section: Binary upgrades > Node count during upgrades
non_blocking.suggestion: 'At most 10% of Nodes per 10 minutes' lets batch k+1 start while batch k is still in the 10%-per-minute ramp, so the count can briefly drop by nearly 20%. Say 'start the next 10% only once `ruralz_control_cluster_nodes` has recovered, about 12 minutes per batch (hypothesis)'. State that the pacing also applies to the rollback rows that return every Node to N-1.

The new process admits each ceiling minus the old process's usage, which is reported each second (target). On a Node near its 20,000-connection ceiling, WebSocket and SSE clients that reconnect after the old process's going-away signals can hit the new process's reduced ceiling before the next report. State that at the ceiling the process delays accepts, which is backpressure within the 1 s report interval, and never refuses, so that ZG-3's 'refuses no new TCP connection' stays true.

'Await near-zero replication lag (target)' gives no number. Give one, for example a replica offset within 1 ms or 1 MiB of the primary (target), so that the L-based bounds in the block below produce concrete figures for a planned failover.

When the largest Plugin `limits.timeout` reaches 23 s or more, the pending-Revision wait exceeds the 60 s ACK timeout (target). In an all-at-once Rollout, every Node then lags together, the batch fails, and the automatic rollback adds a further activation behind the same closing snapshot. Add a validation warning, or cap the timeout that is counted, and mention this cascade.

non_blocking.section: Binary upgrades > Kubernetes Drain and restart
non_blocking.suggestion: Say that the M added Pods also start unqualified, so under derived ceilings the pre-scale adds serving Nodes before the count reflects them. This is within Scalability's lagging-count bound, and it is worth one clause.
Replacing a regional relay, Planned (M4), also restarts the streams of the Nodes it serves. State whether relay replacements follow the same count pacing as replica replacements.
